title: Numbers 7: Five to Ten (a new form on the noun)
description: From five onward, the rule changes again. Пять, шесть, семь, восемь, девять, десять take a different form on the noun: the genitive plural. Today we cover the two cleanest endings: -ов for masculine consonants and the zero ending for feminine -а.
descriptionRussian: С 'пять' начинается новое правило. Числительные 5-10 требуют родительного падежа множественного числа. Сегодня — два самых простых окончания: -ов у мужских согласных и нулевое окончание у женских -а.
intro: Five is where Russian changes its mind. Everything from here up puts the noun into a different form altogether, and the boundary between four and five is arbitrary in the way that only very old grammar can be. There is no logic to recover, and looking for one wastes time. What there is instead is a clean split: a small-number rule you already own, and a large-number rule you learn today. Two rules, one border.
rules: From five onward, the noun goes into the genitive plural. Пять, шесть, семь, восемь, девять, десять all share the same rule.
Pattern 1: masculine consonant nouns add -ов. Студент → студентов, кот → котов, стол → столов.
Pattern 2: feminine -а nouns drop the -а with no replacement (the 'zero ending'). Книга → книг, машина → машин, мама → мам.
The numbers пять-десять have one form each, no gender split (unlike два / две).
Other gen pl endings exist for soft-sign masculines, neuter nouns, and a small set of irregular family-word nouns. Those belong to a future track; today, only the two clean patterns above.
examples: У меня пять книг. (I have five books.) Feminine -а drops: книга → книг.
В классе шесть студентов. (There are six students in the class.) Masculine: -ов on студент.
На столе семь машин. (There are seven toy cars on the table.) Feminine -а drops: машина → машин.
У Антона восемь котов. (Anton has eight cats.) Masculine: -ов on кот.
В доме девять комнат. (There are nine rooms in the house.) Feminine -а drops cleanly: комната → комнат.
У меня десять столов. (I have ten tables.) Masculine: -ов on стол.

tables.title: The Two Clean Gen Pl Patterns

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lesson 6: I have four books.
items.hint: After 2-3-4 the feminine noun takes the genitive singular.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 6. After 'четыре' the noun takes the genitive singular: книги. Today, starting at five, the noun moves into a completely different form: the genitive plural.
Книга is a feminine noun in -а. In the genitive plural that -а simply disappears and the bare stem is left: книг. This is the 'zero ending'. The same rule produces пять мам, пять машин.

items.promptEnglish: There are six students in the class.
items.explanation: Студент is masculine and ends in a hard consonant. The genitive plural adds -ов: студентов. Same ending on кот → котов, стол → столов.
Кот is masculine and ends in a hard consonant, so it takes -ов: котов. The same -ов ending appears on every regular hard-consonant masculine in the gen pl.
Машина is a feminine noun in -а, and the -а disappears: машин.

items.promptEnglish: There are seven tables in the classroom.
items.explanation: Стол is masculine, so it takes -ов: столов. The rule is fully mechanical: hard-consonant masculine + -ов = gen pl. Lock пять/шесть/семь/восемь/девять/десять + this ending and a huge slice of counting takes care of itself.

blanks: У меня десять _____. (I have ten phones.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Телефон is masculine hard consonant. After numbers 5+ the noun is in the genitive plural with -ов: телефонов.

errorCorrection.explanation: From 5 up, the noun takes the genitive plural. For газета that means dropping the -а: пять газет. Газеты is the form for 2-4 (две газеты); at 5 the ending disappears.
After шесть, the noun goes into the GENITIVE PLURAL: уроков (gen pl with the -ов ending, typical for masculine consonant nouns). Урок is the nominative singular, so it cannot follow шесть.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are eight lamps in the house.
errorCorrection.explanation: After восемь (and any 5+), the noun is in the genitive plural: ламп (bare stem, no ending - typical for feminine -а nouns). Лампа is the nominative singular, so it cannot follow восемь.

minimalPairs.explanation: After 5+ the noun is in the gen pl: книг (zero ending). The form 'книги' is the gen sg (used after 2-3-4) and also happens to be the nom pl - the number 'пять' is what forces the gen pl.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There are six students in the class.
minimalPairs.explanation: After 5+ the noun is in the gen pl: студентов. The form 'студента' is the gen sg (used after 2-3-4).

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each phrase by which case the noun is in.

reviewVocab.definition: genitive plural (the form triggered by 5 and above; -ов on masculine consonants, zero ending on feminine -а)
reviewVocab.example: В словосочетании 'пять книг' слово 'книг' стоит в родительном падеже множественного числа с нулевым окончанием.

reviewVocab.definition: zero ending (the gen pl form of a feminine -а noun ends with the bare stem and no suffix)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'мама' имеет нулевое окончание в родительном падеже множественного числа: 'пять мам'.

reviewVocab.definition: the 5+ rule (any number from 5 upward takes the genitive plural on the noun)
reviewVocab.example: По правилу 5+ говорим 'десять студентов', 'пять книг', 'семь столов'.
